data.budget: one session, throwaway git repos, read-only on the ddflow repo
data.claim: Git already provides every transport needed (shared object store makes a contributor commit visible by branch name at once; cherry-pick -x, am -3, bundle, a hidden refs/ddflow/suggest/<item>/<id> namespace, patch-id/range-diff, merge-tree --write-tree as a ~8 ms applicability probe, rerere); ddflow already has the carrier (per-agent local inbox with wake reasons delivered at wait/watch/heartbeat, the ask/approvals engine pattern, drift/sync, merge queue). Missing: a suggestion record + lifecycle, a cheap inbox door at PostToolUse/plugin hooks, drift.relevant/peer notices (DX-merge-fanout-notify, DX-drift-notice open), and an amendment to D-context-sync (an agent may tell only its master). A staged rollout of about 10 task-sized items is possible.
data.falsifier: If more than a few percent of probe-clean suggestions give a red ci on the owner's merge result (semantic conflicts are proven possible in the experiment), or owners do not answer within the TTL for most suggestions, or a suggestion costs the owner more tokens than a lease wait, the protocol is not worth building beyond notify-only.
data.mechanism: Event log is the blackboard (swarm-orchestration.md); a suggestion is a record pointing at a git ref, delivery is a pointer message in the existing inbox; the owner applies by cherry-pick -x (authorship kept, owner's gates cover the tree-keyed result); applied/duplicate state detected by patch-id; staleness by merge-base drift; expiry files an ordinary task via a trigger-style action.
data.probe: git 2.43.0 throwaway repos in the session scratchpad (e1..e10): cherry-pick -x clean/conflict/idempotent, rerere across worktrees, merge --no-ff, format-patch|am -3 in an independent clone, update-ref refs/ddflow namespace + push/fetch refspec, bundle, notes/trailers, patch-id/range-diff/git cherry, merge-tree --write-tree (clean, conflict, timing 5000 files), sync strategies, post-merge rebase (ff, squash, tweaked), semantic clean-merge failure, commit-tree plumbing re-cut, dirty-tree apply; ddflow code read on main 44cc12426: services/inbox.py, api/lifecycle/wait.py+heartbeat.py, api/knowledge/sessions.py, services/lanerelease.py, leasebreak.py, drift.py, ask/engine.py, triggers.py
data.probe_output: merge-tree 6-9 ms clean and conflicting on 5000 files vs 0.92 s scratch-worktree trial merge. am -3 across clones: 'No changes -- Patch already applied', patch-id equal in both repos; fresh empty repo: 'sha1 information is lacking'. git cherry: '-' when applied unchanged, '+' when owner tweaked or squashed; contributor rebase onto main after owner merge: ff -> skipped previously applied; squash -> dropping, patch contents already upstream; tweaked -> conflict. merge-tree CLEAN yet NameError after merge (rename vs new call). Plain clone fetches 0 refs/ddflow; branch -a hides them; git merge S1 'not something we can merge'. Notes do not follow cherry-pick. Stays THEORETICAL: protocol design, token cost, owner response rates, per-harness door behaviour (taken from agent-token-features.md, not re-probed).
data.question: How can agents hand changes and information to each other (suggest a patch to a file's owner, get accept/reject, sync on main/peer progress) on ddflow's event log, git, and harness doors, so long file locks can be broken safely?
